Based on the available information and the options provided in the question, I need to determine the correct formula for the power index (PI) of explosives.

The question states that the power index is calculated using the heat of explosion (Q_ex) and liberated volume of gas (V) of an explosive, relative to picric acid (PA) as a standard reference. 

Looking at the options:
A. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA) · 50
B. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA) · Q_ex
C. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA) · 100

All options have the same base formula (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA), which makes sense as this is comparing the product of heat of explosion and gas volume of the explosive to that of picric acid. The difference is in the multiplication factor.

In explosive science, power indices are typically normalized to make comparisons easier, often using 100 as the reference value for the standard (in this case, picric acid). This would make option C the most likely correct answer.

Final Answer: [ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
